findings.title: A CT plane demonstrated in more than one pass inherited the first pass’s daughter identity
findings.reproduction: Lesson 4 (vertical, right-upper-apical.junction-14.pattern), second demonstration pass through slice 419: the drawn model course locator was Daughter B · RB1a while the caption named Daughter A · RB1b.
findings.rootCause: frames walks the parent interval once per daughter, so slice 419 is authored steps 18, 25 and 62 of 68. LocalCtLesson resolved the displayed frame with frames.findIndex((f) => f.slice === displayedSlice) and the overlay frame with frames.find(...), which always answer with the first step showing that plane. modelCourseLocators() derives the pass from the frame index, so the drawn crosshair (from s.frame) was correct while the caption, the course-locator sentence and the "n of N" position came from the earlier pass. Generic, not specific to Lesson 4: Lesson 8 gave Daughter B’s pass the lead-in’s "Approach context, slice 332" caption and its "Approach · LLL and Parent · LB6" locator names.
findings.repair: New engine/model-course.ts helper demonstrationFrameIndex(frames, currentIndex, slice): the current step wins whenever its plane is on screen, otherwise the occurrence nearest the current step does. Used by LocalCtLesson for the overlay frame, the displayed caption/position and onViewChange. Identity is keyed on the authored demonstration step, never on a slice number.
findings.rotationReflectionChecked: Covered in the Jest regression: rotating the CT to the regional tracing view and returning to standard axial leaves the caption, the transport position and the locator aria-label unchanged.

findings.title: The explanation for an intentionally suppressed wall label was covered by the canvas
findings.reproduction: Lesson 8 (orientation-changes), second LB6 example (left-lower-returning.junction-25.integration), slice 345: Daughter B is correctly withheld from the wall because its projected point is occluded, the sentence saying so is in the DOM, and document.elementFromPoint returned the <canvas> at every point down that sentence. Reproduced at 1427x1226, 390x844 and 320x740.
findings.rootCause: .pairedScope was aspect-ratio: 1 with position: relative and .pairedScope .clinicalCanvas was position: absolute; inset: 0. The explanation is an in-flow sibling of that canvas, so it was laid out inside the same square and painted beneath an opaque positioned element at every width.
findings.repair: .pairedScope is a flex column; the canvas keeps its square with aspect-ratio: 1 in normal flow (still position: relative so the opening-letter SVG overlay covers the camera exactly); the explanation takes its own space beneath it. Loading, surface-error and 3D-boundary paragraphs reserve the same square so mounting the canvas shifts nothing.
notChanged: the ray cast and its occlusion result
the suppression rule (Daughter B is still not drawn on the wall)
